AIVC Launches With $112 Million in Strategic Investment to Build AI-Focused Companies
November 23, 2026
AIVC (AI Value Creation) has emerged from stealth with $112 million in strategic investment , backed by a family office and members of its leadership team, to support artificial intelligence-driven business transformation and the development of new companies.
The investment will fund AIVC’s operations across three interconnected activities: transforming existing businesses through AI, developing reusable technology based on those engagements and launching independent companies through its venture studio.
A majority of the capital will be allocated to AIVC’s Studio, which plans to establish three to five companies annually. The firm intends to identify commercial opportunities through its work with existing businesses before committing resources to new ventures.
AIVC was founded by RC Willenbrock, its chief executive officer and a former partner and head of AIxPE at Boston Consulting Group. David Sukhin, previously head of AI at Citadel, leads the firm’s venture studio.
The company has assembled a team of operators, engineers and research scientists with experience at Citadel, Millennium, Palantir, BCG, Nike, Lemonade, Airbnb and American Express.
Unlike traditional consulting firms that primarily provide advisory services, AIVC combines operational execution with technology development and company ownership. Its model is designed to link compensation and investment returns to measurable business outcomes rather than the volume of AI technology deployed.
“AI is a compression engine: it shrinks the time and effort that routine work consumes,” said Willenbrock. “But whether that reaches the bottom line depends on what a company does with the capacity it frees. We do not want AI to replace what makes people valuable. We want it to make people more human.”
The firm’s approach emphasizes using AI to automate routine processes while redirecting employee capacity toward higher-value activities, customer service and business growth.
Within its venture studio, AIVC plans to develop companies around commercial problems identified and tested through its operating engagements. The strategy is intended to establish customer demand and technical feasibility before launching new businesses.
“The two hardest parts of building new companies are (1) knowing which problems deserve to become a company and (2) identifying the most exceptional people to solve them,” said Sukhin.
AIVC said its current engagements are on pace to generate more than $1 billion in enterprise value, primarily through business growth and increased operating capacity rather than workforce reductions. That figure represents the firm’s projected value creation, not realized investment returns or independently verified financial results.
The company said it will prioritize engagements where potential financial benefits can be measured and where clients are prepared to implement and sustain operational changes.
AIVC did not disclose the identity of its family office investor, the ownership stakes associated with the $112 million investment or the valuation assigned to the company.

Ant Group Leads $100 Million Funding for China's Simplexity Robotics
By: Asia Business Outlook Team | Monday, 23 November 2026
Chinese robotics startup Simplexity Robotics has raised $100 million in funding in a round led by Ant Group , as major technology companies continue to invest in artificial intelligence (AI) and humanoid robots .
The latest funding round values the company at $1.6 billion, according to chairman and co-founder Wang Kai, who shared the details with Bloomberg News.
The funding round also includes investments from Alibaba Group , Tencent Holdings , HongShan Capital and Lanchi Ventures.
The amount contributed by each investor has not been disclosed. The investment comes as Chinese companies increase their focus on physical AI , which allows robots to understand their surroundings and perform tasks in the real world.
Key Highlights
Ant Group Leads $100 Million Funding Round for China's Simplexity Robotics
Simplexity Robotics Raises $100 Million at $1.6 Billion Valuation
Alibaba and Tencent Back Simplexity Robotics in $100 Million Funding Round
Ant Group Leads $100 Million Investment in Simplexity Robotics
Simplexity Robotics is a Chinese startup working on physical AI technology for robots. Based in Suzhou, the company is looking to strengthen its position in China's growing humanoid robotics market .
The latest $100 million funding round values the company at $1.6 billion. Ant Group led the investment, while Alibaba, Tencent, HongShan Capital and Lanchi Ventures also participated. However, the company has not shared details about how much each investor contributed or how it plans to use the funds.
Physical AI is becoming an important area in robotics as companies work to develop machines that can understand their surroundings and perform tasks with less human involvement. Unlike traditional robots that follow fixed instructions, these systems are designed to respond to changes and make decisions based on what they observe.
Developing such technology requires improvements in both hardware and software. Robots need to move, handle objects and respond to different situations, while AI systems help them understand instructions and carry out tasks. This has encouraged technology companies and investors to pay more attention to the sector.
China's Robotics Sector Sees Growing Investor Interest
The investment comes at a time when China's robotics industry has started to see a slowdown in funding. According to Bloomberg, fundraising in the sector fell to around $1.6 billion in October, a significant drop from the peak recorded in June.
Despite the slowdown, major technology companies continue to invest in startups working on robotics and AI. Ant Group, which is backed by Alibaba co-founder Jack Ma, has been expanding its interest in emerging technologies. Its latest investment brings it together with Alibaba and Tencent in backing Simplexity Robotics.
China has become an important market for robot development , with several startups and established technology companies working on machines for industrial and other commercial uses. However, developing robots that can perform tasks reliably outside controlled environments remains a challenge.

articles.title: Compuvi Reaches $50 Million Valuation Following Consulta Ventures Investment
articles.snippet:
Compuvi has reached a $50 million post-money valuation after securing an investment from Consulta Ventures through a pre-Series A bridge round.
The post Compuvi Reaches $50 Million Valuation Following Consulta Ventures Investment appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Compuvi Reaches $50 Million Valuation Following Consulta Ventures Investment
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:55 AM
Compuvi Reaches $50 Million Valuation Following Consulta Ventures Investment
Compuvi has reached a $50 million post-money valuation after securing an investment from Consulta Ventures through a pre-Series A bridge round.
The San Francisco-based enterprise AI company plans to use the investment and Consulta’s strategic support to strengthen its global commercial operations, sales organization, and customer success infrastructure. Compuvi will also continue developing its technology as it prepares for a Series A financing.
Expanding Preventive Compliance Technology
Compuvi develops Confinaid, an AI-powered platform designed to identify potential legal and regulatory risks within corporate communications, documents, and workflows before violations occur.
The platform analyzes the context of emails, enterprise messages, and documents to identify risks involving areas such as competition law, data protection, employment law, and financial regulation. Confinaid can alert employees in real time, route potentially problematic content to legal or compliance teams, and prevent certain communications from being sent.
Unlike conventional compliance tools that rely heavily on keywords or detect violations after they happen, Confinaid applies contextual analysis to support a preventive approach.
Consulta’s involvement will extend beyond financial backing. Its partners will work with Compuvi to develop scalable sales processes and customer success capabilities while helping the company expand its enterprise customer base in the United States and Europe.
Compuvi has approximately 20 employees across the United States, Europe, and Türkiye. Its customers operate in regulated industries including financial services, healthcare, retail, telecommunications, energy, and legal services.
KEY QUOTES:
“What Consulta and Compuvi have in common is that we understand the importance of the problem we are addressing not only in theory, but through its real impact on business processes. Compliance is becoming an increasingly critical management priority for organizations. We are developing a new approach that makes it possible to address risks before they emerge, rather than managing them after the fact.”
“Consulta’s firsthand experience of this need and its confidence in our solution make this collaboration particularly meaningful to us. By working together, we will build stronger and more scalable sales, marketing and customer success operations. We believe this investment will make an important contribution to our long-term strategic roadmap. In the coming period, our focus will be on accelerating our growth in global markets as we prepare for our Series A.”
Ataberk Ciftlikli, Founder and CEO of Compuvi

articles.title: Vigor Marine Wins Contract Worth Up To $45.4 Million For USNS Lucy Stone Work
articles.snippet:
Military Sealift Command has awarded Vigor Marine a $39.1 million firm-fixed-price contract for post-shakedown work on the fleet replenishment oiler USNS Lucy Stone.
The post Vigor Marine Wins Contract Worth Up To $45.4 Million For USNS Lucy Stone Work appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Vigor Marine Wins Contract Worth Up To $45.4 Million For USNS Lucy Stone Work
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:57 AM
Vigor Marine Wins Contract Worth Up To $45.4 Million For USNS Lucy Stone Work
Military Sealift Command has awarded Vigor Marine a $39.1 million firm-fixed-price contract for post-shakedown work on the fleet replenishment oiler USNS Lucy Stone.
The base contract covers a 137-calendar-day shipyard availability following the vessel’s initial operational period. Five unexercised options could increase the contract’s total cumulative value to approximately $45.4 million.
Post-Shakedown Availability
Post-shakedown availabilities are conducted after newly delivered vessels have completed initial operations and testing. The work commonly addresses deficiencies discovered during that period and completes repairs, modifications, inspections, and adjustments needed to prepare a ship for sustained service.
The award announcement did not provide a detailed list of the individual tasks Vigor will perform on USNS Lucy Stone.
Work will be conducted at Vigor’s facilities in Portland, Oregon, beginning January 18, 2027. The availability is scheduled to conclude on June 3, 2027.
The Navy obligated the full $39.1 million base-contract value at the time of the award using fiscal 2027 operations-and-maintenance funding. Those funds are scheduled to expire at the end of the current fiscal year.
The approximately $6.3 million associated with the five options has not been obligated. That additional value would only become funded contract work if Military Sealift Command exercises the applicable options.
The firm-fixed-price structure establishes an agreed amount for the base scope, placing responsibility on Vigor to perform the specified work within that price, subject to any government-authorized changes.
The government competed the procurement through its contracting portal and received two proposals.
Military Sealift Command in Norfolk, Virginia, is the contracting activity. The contract number is N3220527C0005.

articles.title: Korte Construction Wins $38 Million Fort Gordon Barracks Contract
articles.snippet:
The U.S. Army has awarded Korte Construction a $38 million contract to replace existing facilities with two new barracks at Fort Gordon, Georgia.
The post Korte Construction Wins $38 Million Fort Gordon Barracks Contract appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Korte Construction Wins $38 Million Fort Gordon Barracks Contract
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:39 AM
Korte Construction Wins $38 Million Fort Gordon Barracks Contract
The U.S. Army has awarded Korte Construction a $38 million contract to replace existing facilities with two new barracks at Fort Gordon, Georgia.
The fixed-price-award-fee contract uses a design-build-to-budget delivery approach. Its scope includes demolishing existing infrastructure and designing and constructing the two replacement barracks.
Military Housing Modernization
All work will be performed at Fort Gordon, with completion expected by September 26, 2029.
The Army obligated the contract’s entire $38 million value at the time of the award using fiscal 2027 military-construction funding. This means the announced value represents funded work rather than an unfunded maximum ceiling.
The procurement attracted 13 bids, indicating substantial competition for the construction project. Korte’s award was one of the more heavily competed projects included in the supplied group of military contracts.
The project will replace aging facilities with two modern barracks intended to support the Army’s service-member housing requirements at Fort Gordon. The award announcement did not disclose the planned square footage, resident capacity, configuration, or amenities of the new buildings.
Under the design-build-to-budget approach, the project’s design and construction will be coordinated within the Army’s established funding limit. This model is intended to align the final design with available resources while allowing construction considerations to be incorporated earlier in project development.
The fixed-price-award-fee structure establishes a defined contract price while allowing Korte to earn additional fees based on performance criteria established by the government. These criteria can include areas such as quality, cost control, schedule management, and overall contract execution.
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ Savannah District is the contracting activity. The contract number is W912HN-27-C-A004.
